label: Codex
description: One conversation with Codex, OpenAI's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Codex runs on your machine (a local install only) with your own login, working in `folder`, from your own install of `codex` when there is one on PATH; when there is none, weft installs Codex itself, once, into a folder of its own shared by every program on the machine. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. Its model is always named: left out, it is the one Codex lists as the default for the login, never the one a machine's own `config.toml` names, which a plan may refuse. A ChatGPT login is kept alive by weft, never by Codex: every Codex node on one connection gets the same fresh token, and when it is about to die or is refused this node asks weft for a new one, which it hears on `stream`, so wire `stream` into every AskAgent. While one of your tools is unanswered, Codex asks its model again every half minute or so, so a tool that waits on a person costs model requests while it waits: put a person behind `question` instead. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission policy, the sandbox, the model, the reasoning effort and a system prompt to append; the rest of Codex's own settings stay in its `config.toml`. Your program's tools reach Codex under their plain names. A tool named like one of its own that Codex can turn off by itself (`web_search`, `view_image`, `update_plan`, `image_generation`) takes that one's place; a name it cannot give up alone (`apply_patch`, its shell's `exec_command`, `shell_command` and `write_stdin`, its goal tools, `request_plugin_install`, and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built, and so is a name Codex keeps for itself: one starting `mcp__`, or holding a character other than a letter, a digit, `_` or `-`.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Codex in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A CodexAccess's `access`: your ChatGPT login file (on a local install) or an API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Codex uses the login already on it (`codex login`).

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Codex works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Codex program to run, when it is not the `codex` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: When Codex asks before acting. `ask`: before anything it does not already trust, every request coming out of AskAgent as a question. `on_request`: when the model decides to ask. `never`: it never asks, and the sandbox decides what it can do. `bypass`: it never asks and has no sandbox; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The model Codex uses (`gpt-6-luna`, ...). Left out, the one Codex lists as the default for its login.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Reasoning effort
inputs.description: How hard the model reasons each turn: one of the efforts the model offers (`low`, `medium`, `high`, and for some models more). Left out, the model's default.

inputs.name: sandbox
inputs.label: Sandbox
inputs.description: What Codex's commands may touch on your machine: `read_only`, `workspace_write` (the folder and nothing outside it) or `full_access`. In a computer there is no sandbox to run (no bubblewrap), so it has full access there, the computer being the wall, and this changes nothing.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: appendSystemPrompt
inputs.label: Add to the system prompt
inputs.description: Instructions added to Codex's own, for the whole conversation.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: Codex '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
Codex '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a CodexAccess on `access`.
Codex '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
Codex '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, on_request, never, bypass.
Codex '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
Codex '{id}' has a `sandbox` it does not know; pick one of read_only, workspace_write, full_access.
Codex '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Codex itself.
